criterion: Recovery / Dead ends: every screen offers the obvious next step
description: On the signed-out screen, Check again only re-reads /session. It can never sign this browser in, yet it is the only action offered, and its first click removes the expired-link notice so the screen looks as if something changed.
expected: The action either does something that can work (e.g. explains/copies the exact command, or offers a way to request a new link) or the notice persists and Check again reports "Still not signed in".
actual: Three clicks each produce GET /session 401; the notice disappears after the first; no feedback after the second and third.
suggested_fix: Keep the failure notice until sign-in succeeds; after a failed check show "Still not signed in" inline; relabel to make clear it only detects a sign-in made elsewhere.

description: The signed-out copy assumes an agent ("Ask your agent to open Pardner for you") and never says the person can run the command themselves, nor that the launcher always targets the default browser so a second browser needs `pardner open --output-file FILE` and pasting the URL here.
expected: Copy covering both: run `pardner open` yourself (or ask your agent); for a different browser, use --output-file and paste the link into this tab.
actual: Only the agent route is mentioned; the second-browser route is undiscoverable from the UI.
suggested_fix: Rewrite the paragraph and add a one-line "Using a different browser?" hint.

criterion: Component consistency: same instruction worded the same everywhere
description: The signed-out screen names `pardner client open`; the startup shell and config-failure screen name `pardner open`.
suggested_fix: Use `pardner open` everywhere a person reads it.

description: Inline `pardner client open` on the signed-out screen renders in a Courier-like serif monospace (the static shell uses a modern sans monospace) and wraps mid-command at 1440px ("pardner client" / "open").
expected: One monospace stack across the app; command kept on one line (white-space: nowrap).
actual: Visibly different code font; command split across two lines.
suggested_fix: Apply the shared code font-family to `code` in the client screens and `white-space: nowrap` on short commands.

description: A reused link and an unused-but-expired (>60s) link show the identical notice; the 60-second lifetime is never stated.
expected: "Sign-in links work once and expire after a minute."
actual: "already used or has expired" for both, with no lifetime.
suggested_fix: State the lifetime in the notice.
